newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Treasury Feb oper deficit at 308 mln reais.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Treasury Feb oper deficit at 308 mln reais.

text.p: Brazil's Treasury said its operational budget deficit was 308 million reais in February, bringing the year-to-date operational deficit to 1.669 billion reais, or 1.32 percent of gross domestic product.
In the same period last year, the Treasury posted a 3.295 billion real operational budget deficit, equivalent to 2.72 percent of GDP, it said in a statement.
The operational budget includes debt servicing costs.
The Treasury's primary account, which does not include interest payments, showed a surplus of 894 million reais in February, compared to a 407 million real deficit in January.

In the first two months of 1997, Treasury showed a primary surplus of 487 million reais, or 0.25 percent of GDP, compared with a deficit equivalent to 1.1 percent of GDP in the January-February 1996 period.
The Treasury said its nominal deficit, which includes interest payments and adjusts for foreign exchange fluctuations, stood at 980 million reais in February.
The January-February 1997 nominal deficit was 3.725 billion reais, or 2.94 percent of GDP, it said.
The Treasury said receipts in February totaled 7.864 billion reais, 15 percent up from February 1996 primarily due to the levy of a new CPMF financial transaction tax, which raised 517 million reais.
Treasury also said February's improvement was caused by lower payroll costs compared with January, when a bonus equivalent to a month's salary was paid to federal workers.

In addition, the Treasury said its net debt stood at 140.946 billion reais at the end of February, or 17.7 percent of GDP. Of that total, 85.111 billion reais was internal debt, while 55.835 billion reais was external debt.
In February, the Treasury's stock of net debt grew 5.2 percent from January and was 41.3 percent higher than in February 1996.
